name: Reclamation_PumpingPlants
title: Reclamation Pumping Plants
description:
This GIS layer represents the spatial locations and key attributes of pumping plants owned, operated, or managed by the Bureau of Reclamation. It is part of the Enterprise Asset Registry used to support infrastructure asset management, water delivery operations, and energy planning. Each feature in the layer corresponds to a pumping plant facility and includes associated metadata such as asset name, associated project or system, region, pump type, horsepower, and ownership status. The dataset is maintained by Reclamation’s Asset Management Office and is periodically updated to reflect changes in infrastructure inventory and operational status.

Definitions

Pumping Plant: A facility associated with a water conveyance system that is designed to convey water from one location to another by introducing mechanical energy to raise the hydraulic grade line. Pumps associated with water treatment plants, wastewater treatment plants, wells, pump-generating plants, fish facilities, dewatering pumps, and sewage lift stations are not considered pumping plants.

Major Pumping Plant: Combined horsepower equal to or greater than 2,500.

Minor Pumping Plant: Combined horsepower of less than 2,500.
snippet: The objective of the Pumping Plant Asset Class is to establish a single authoritative source in GIS format for Reclamation's entire inventory of pumping plants and implement processes and procedures for maintaining the inventory into the future.
